title: After US exit, Iran gains space in Iraq and a harder balancing act
gist: With the US Operation Inherent Resolve mission in Iraq ending Sept. 30, 2026 after more than 12 years, Iran's Quds Force chief Esmail Qaani hailed a 'humiliating removal' and demanded full US expulsion, but the analysis argues Tehran now faces the harder task of converting the vacuum into durable influence and reviving allied militias after a war year that decimated its regional network.

themes.theme: End of US military mission in Iraq

insights.claim: The US withdrawal from Iraq was completed on Sept. 30, 2026, ending the Iraq-based military mission of Operation Inherent Resolve after more than 12 years.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran
insights.so_what: Removal of the US military footprint changes Iraq's security balance and the risk calculus for regional energy and investment exposure.
insights.quote: The US withdrawal was completed Sept. 30, ending the Iraq-based military mission of Operation Inherent Resolve after more than 12 years.
insights.locator: And the timing makes the symbolism

insights.claim: IRGC Quds Force chief Brig. Gen. Esmail Qaani described the US pull-out as a 'humiliating removal', credited Iraqi militias with forcing Washington out, and insisted the remaining American presence — on land and in the sky — must also be expelled.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran
insights.so_what: Tehran signals it will keep pressuring residual US presence (including airspace access), sustaining risk of militia attacks on remaining US assets.
insights.quote: "America must be expelled from Iraq, both from its land and from its sky,"
insights.locator: TEHRAN — Iran's top regional military commander

insights.claim: Tehran sees the US withdrawal not merely as an Iraqi sovereignty matter but as part of a deeper regional contest in which the US has been under sustained pressure from Iran and its allied armed groups.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran
insights.so_what: Iran will present the exit as a strategic victory, which may embolden its proxies' posture elsewhere.
insights.quote: Tehran is not treating the end of the US military mission simply as an Iraqi sovereignty issue.
insights.locator: Tehran is not treating the end

themes.theme: Iran's weakened network and harder balancing act

insights.claim: The US exit came after a devastating year of war involving Iran, Israel and the United States in which Tehran's regional network was decimated, its military capabilities severely hit and its power-projection ability under unprecedented pressure.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran
insights.so_what: Iran is gaining space in Iraq from a position of weakness, limiting its capacity to exploit the vacuum quickly.
insights.quote: Tehran's regional network was decimated, its military capabilities severely hit
insights.locator: And the timing makes the symbolism

insights.claim: For Iran, getting Washington out may have been the easier part; it now has to turn the US absence into durable influence and revive allied militias without provoking instability in Iraq.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran
insights.so_what: Contrary to a simple 'Iran wins' reading, the vacuum carries risks for Tehran; instability in Iraq could rebound against Iranian interests.
insights.quote: the easier part may have been getting Washington out, but it may now have to struggle turning the absence into durable influence

insights.claim: The symbolism of the withdrawal is especially important to Tehran because of its timing, coming right after its regional setbacks.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran
insights.so_what: Expect Iranian messaging to lean heavily on the exit as a morale and legitimacy boost for its axis.
insights.quote: And the timing makes the symbolism particularly important.
insights.locator: And the timing makes the symbolism
